scenes.heading: Data Lake Architecture
scenes.narration: A data lake stores raw and refined data at scale on cheap object storage, organized into progressive quality zones.

scenes.heading: The layered zones
bullets: Open formats keep the lake engine-agnostic.
scenes.narration: The bronze zone preserves raw data exactly as it arrived, giving an auditable source of truth. Silver applies cleaning, validation, and conforming so the data becomes trustworthy. Gold holds curated, aggregated tables ready for analytics, and open file formats let many engines read the same lake.

scenes.heading: Data's journey through the lake
scenes.narration: New data lands first in the bronze zone untouched, so nothing is lost. Cleaning and validation promote it to silver, where it is reliable and conformed. Business logic then aggregates it into gold tables, which serve dashboards, reports, and machine learning.

scenes.heading: Data lake vs warehouse

left.title: Data lake
points: Great for raw and ML data

scenes.narration: A data lake accepts any format and applies structure only when read, making it cheap and flexible for raw and semi-structured data. A warehouse enforces schema up front and excels at fast, governed SQL analytics. The lakehouse pattern increasingly blends both by adding table formats over lake storage.

scenes.text: A data lake uses layered bronze, silver, and gold zones on open storage to turn raw data into trusted, business-ready datasets.
scenes.narration: The zoned architecture lets you keep everything cheaply while still delivering clean, curated data to consumers.
